trace.msg: Let's look at this puzzle carefully. I'll only move when I can explain why.
Number 2 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going up-right would strand number 3: it would be left with only one free neighbour. So the line goes down-right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up-right.
Going up-right would force the line onto number 11 before its turn. So the line goes left.
I can't rule out up-left or left yet, so I'll make an educated guess: up-left.
Number 7 is only reachable this way.
Number 8 is next and right here, so the line takes it.
Going up-left would cut off the right side (8 cells); going up-right would cut off the right side (7 cells) (and 1 more option fails too). So the line goes down-right.

Going up-right would strand number 10: it would be left with only one free neighbour; going right would strand number 10: it would be left with only one free neighbour (and 1 more option fails too). So the line goes down-left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes right.

Going up-right would leave both cell (3,-2) and cell (3,0) needing the line next, and it can't do both; going right would turn number 11 into a dead-end pocket with no way out. So the line goes down-right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes up-right.
Going left, the next 5 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (-1,-1). So the line goes down-left.
Going left, the next 4 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (-1,-1). So the line goes up-left.
Going down-left, the next 3 moves are forced and the line gets stuck at cell (-1,-1). So the line goes left.
Going down-right, every way of continuing runs into a dead end within a few moves. So the line goes down-left.
Going down-right, the next move is forced and the line gets stuck at cell (0,-2). So the line goes right.
Going down-left leaves no safe move afterwards. So the line goes down-right.
The line must go left: down-left is number 18, which comes later.

Going left would turn number 16 into a dead-end pocket with no way out; going down-left would strand number 16: it would be left with only one free neighbour (and 1 more option fails too). So the line goes up-left.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down-left.
Going right would force the line onto number 18 before its turn. So the line goes down-right.
Going right would force the line onto number 20 before its turn. So the line goes up-right.
Going right would turn number 18 into a dead-end pocket with no way out; going down-right would force the line onto number 20 before its turn. So the line goes up-right.
Only one free cell next to the line, so it goes down-right.
Going down-left would leave both number 19 and number 20 needing the line next, and it can't do both. So the line goes down-right.
The line must go left: down-left is number 21, which comes later.
Every cell is covered and the numbers are in order. Case closed!
I grow a search tree: my policy network suggests moves, a trained value head judge them. 48 simulations per move.
One of my simulated futures reached the end after 13 simulations. Following it!
Let evolution do the work: 24 random lines compete, the fittest breed and mutate.
Generation 0: the best random line covers 29/37 cells (78%).
Generation 2: fitness 23/37. The best line covers 35 cells, the first 23 of them still look solvable.
Generation 4: fitness 37/37. The best line covers 37 cells.
Generation 4: a perfect line evolved! Every cell covered.
Feeling lucky! Before every move I'll play 24 random futures and bet on the move that survives most often.
Jackpot! A future after going down-right covers the whole board. Cashing in!
Let x(cell, step) mean 'this cell is step number <step> of the line'. 37 cells x 37 steps, minus everything that's impossible at a glance.
Encoded 3,000 variables and 8,128 clauses in 0.00 s (785 position variables survive the pruning).
Solver found a model in 0.00 s. Decoding it into a line...
Q.E.D. Every clause is satisfied.
